In fetch_error_details the code builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) which returns a dict keyed by node_id, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()). Dict values order is not guaranteed to match error_ids order, and missing keys shrink values. The result pairs the wrong title/message/timestamp with the wrong error id. Consequence is wrong error context merged into replay breadcrumb logs sent to Seer, producing misleading AI summaries.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flagged table visualization discards real query results

When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization the code renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns={[]} and tableData {data:[], meta:{fields:{}, units:{}}} instead of using result.data, result.meta, fields, and fieldAliases computed above. Consequence is dashboards behind the flag show empty tables regardless of query results.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Age/timestamp exclusivity uses truthiness and neither is required

validate_timestamp checks if self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks get("timestamp"). Values of 0 are falsy, so a report with age=0 plus timestamp or timestamp=0 plus age incorrectly passes, and both age and timestamp are optional so a report with neither also passes. The Reporting specs require exactly one of age or timestamp. Consequence is invalid reports are accepted and mixed-spec reports with zero values are not rejected.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Analytics recorded before feature and validation checks

analytics.record for preprod_artifact.api.assemble runs before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before schema, missing-chunk, and state validation. Every POST including disabled-feature, malformed, and unauthorized calls is counted. Consequence is inflated assemble metrics and stored organization/project/user ids for requests that should not count.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

false_positives.candidate:
Attribute-keys query key omits organization and changes caching

The refactor replaces useApiQuery with path /organizations/<slug>/trace-items/attributes/ with useQuery keyed only as ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions] where queryOptions has no org slug. Switching organizations reuses the prior org cached TagCollection. It also drops staleTime 0, refetchOnWindowFocus false, and retry false. Consequence is stale cross-org attribute suggestions and extra retries and refetches.

Column fallback crashes when meta is missing

The fallback does Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields) and tableData?.meta.fields[key]. The optional chain only guards tableData, not meta. If tableData is undefined or has no meta, this throws TypeError. Consequence is dashboard or story rendering an empty or loading table crashes instead of rendering empty.

Merged-PR template calls truncate on wrong class

The diff defines _truncate_title as a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration but get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title. PRCommentWorkflow is not the class defining the helper in this file. If PRCommentWorkflow does not provide that method this raises NameError/AttributeError at runtime. Consequence is suspect-issues PR comment generation for GitHub and GitLab crashes and no comment is posted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code match is case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive

Generated codes are lowercase hex but displayed with placeholder XXXXX-XXXXX and formatted with a dash, so users will naturally type uppercase or paste with spaces/newlines. The code only does replaceAll("-","") and indexOf, with no toLowerCase() or trim(). A correct code typed in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace fails with IncorrectBackupCode, causing false lockout. Same pattern exists in the disable endpoint. Normalize case and whitespace before comparison.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code single-use check has TOCTOU race

Login does read-decrypt-indexOf-encrypt-write as separate steps: it reads backupCodes, finds the index, sets that slot to null, and writes back. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both read the same array before either writes, both find the code, and both succeed. This allows replay of a supposedly single-use backup code. The consume must be atomic via transaction, row lock, or optimistic concurrency.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code login can bypass password check

authorize() skips password verification when credentials.totpCode is truthy, but takes the backup-code branch whenever credentials.backupCode is truthy. An attacker who knows a victim's email and one valid backup code can send password=wrong, totpCode=anything, backupCode=valid. The password check is skipped because totpCode is present, the backup-code check succeeds, and login returns success. This reduces 2FA to single-factor (backup code only) and allows account takeover without the password. Password must be verified for CAL users regardless of second-factor fields.

No test for backup-code login or disable

The PR adds backup-code generation, login via credentials provider, and disable via backup code, including single-use invalidation and new error codes. The e2e file explicitly leaves TODO for login + disabling with backup and only asserts download filename and copy toast. There is no automated proof that a valid backup code logs in, that reuse fails, or that disable with backup works, leaving the critical auth paths uncovered.

Non-string backupCode crashes disable endpoint

The handler guards only truthiness of req.body.backupCode then unconditionally calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll. If a client sends a truthy non-string JSON value such as a number, array, or object, replaceAll throws TypeError, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' before string operations.

OAuth/SAML users blocked from using backup codes

The early guards throw ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled and IncorrectEmailPassword when credentials.totpCode is missing, without considering credentials.backupCode. A Google/SAML user with 2FA who loses their authenticator and submits only email+backupCode via the lost-access UI will always hit the third-party error and can never use a backup code. The checks must also accept backupCode as satisfying the second-factor presence.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent fallback can never match, calendarId becomes undefined

In updateEvent selectedCalendar is externalCalendarId when truthy else event.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). When the else branch runs externalCalendarId is falsy (null/undefined/''), so comparing stored externalIds to a falsy value never matches and the result is always undefined. Updates without an externalCalendarId therefore call Google with calendarId undefined instead of falling back to the destination calendar, causing update failures.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Calendar.createEvent now requires credentialId, breaking implementations

The Calendar interface changed to createEvent(event, credentialId: number) with required second param, but Lark, Office365 and CalDAV implementations still declare createEvent(event) only. Callers passing only one arg get undefined credentialId at runtime, and third-party Calendar implementations will fail type-check. The param should be optional or all implementations updated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateAllCalendarEvents reuses stale credential across references

In updateAllCalendarEvents credential is declared outside the for loop and only reassigned when a lookup succeeds. If a reference has a credentialId that is found in neither memory nor DB, credential keeps the value from the previous iteration (or undefined on first). The code then calls updateEvent with the wrong credential, updating the wrong user's calendar and leaving the intended calendar stale, or throwing when undefined.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

false_positives.candidate:
Collective hosts dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar

handleNewBooking initializes evt.destinationCalendar to null when neither eventType nor organizer has one, then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) for COLLECTIVE events. Optional chaining on null is a no-op, so second hosts' destinationCalendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded and those hosts never get calendar events.

Google Meet fallback crashes when no destinationCalendar

EventManager.create does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] then reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null or empty the destructured value is undefined, so accessing .integration throws TypeError and crashes booking creation for Google Meet events without a destination calendar. It should be mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

createEvent patch ignores primary fallback

createEvent inserts with calendarId selectedCalendar || 'primary' but the follow-up patch for hangoutLink uses raw selectedCalendar. When no destination matches credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined, so insert goes to primary while patch is sent with undefined calendarId and fails, leaving the description without the hangout link.

destinationCalendar changed from single object to array, breaking webhooks

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from DestinationCalendar|null to DestinationCalendar[]|null. Webhook payloads, emails and any external consumers expecting an object or null now receive an array. The e2e file shows the inconsistency: some triggers still expect null while BOOKING_REJECTED now expects [], proving the contract is both breaking and inconsistent across code paths that return null vs [].

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Placeholder refresh_token overwrites real refresh token

parseRefreshTokenResponse injects refresh_token='refresh_token' literal when missing. The PR docs say the external sync endpoint returns only access_token and expiry. Callers in Office365, Zoom and Webex persist that object, overwriting the valid stored refresh_token with the dummy string and permanently destroying the ability to refresh via the provider.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Lenient token schema uses broken computed keys and strips fields

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] as object keys, which evaluates to a literal string like Zod object toString, not a wildcard. Zod by default strips unknown keys, so expiry_date, expires_in, instance_url, signature and other required fields are dropped. Downstream merges then lose expiry and Salesforce loses instance_url, corrupting credentials.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stores Zod safeParse wrapper instead of token data

In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full safeParse result {success, data}. The code stores that wrapper as credential.key instead of .data. The next load via googleCredentialSchema.parse will fail because the stored shape is {success,data} not tokens, corrupting Google credentials after first refresh.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync path returns fetch Response but code expects .data

When credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response. Google code does res?.data expecting a Gaxios response with .data. fetch Response has no .data, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError, breaking Google refresh for all sync-enabled users.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync path returns fetch Response but code expects .data

When credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response. Google code does res?.data expecting a Gaxios response with .data. fetch Response has no .data, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError, breaking Google refresh for all sync-enabled users.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Passes credentialId as calcomUserId to sync endpoint

zoho-bigin refreshAccessToken receives credentialId which is credential.id and passes it as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, which sends it as calcomUserId. The sync endpoint will look up the wrong user or fail, returning wrong tokens. It should pass credential.userId like all other calendar services.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Checks statusText instead of status code

Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText !== 'OK' to detect failure. statusText is an optional reason phrase that varies by server and is often empty. It should check !response.ok or response.status. The current check causes false failures or missed failures.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Returns connection with stale tokens after refresh

After refreshing and updating the DB with accessTokenParsed.data, Salesforce getClient builds the jsforce.Connection from the old credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url instead of the new tokens. All subsequent Salesforce calls use the expired token until the credential is reloaded.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unhandled Zod decrypt and JSON errors return 500

The webhook calls zod .parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse without try/catch. Invalid body, wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext throws and results in unhandled 500 instead of 400, and can crash the handler. It should use safeParse and handle decrypt failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Assumes axios shape but sync path returns fetch Response

Bigin code does tokenInfo.data.error assuming an axios response. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response which has no .data, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and accessing .error throws TypeError, breaking Bigin refresh in sync mode.

Assumes axios shape but sync path returns fetch Response

Zohocrm code does zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error assuming axios. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response with no .data, so .data.error throws TypeError. The sync response is never parsed via .json(), breaking Zoho CRM refresh.

Bypasses sync helper yet uses lenient schema

Unlike every other service, Salesforce getClient always fetches Salesforce directly and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so sync mode is ineffective. Worse, when sharing is enabled parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the lenient schema that strips instance_url/signature/scope, and the truncated object is persisted, corrupting Salesforce credentials.

Find-then-create race can duplicate credentials

The webhook does findFirst then update or create as two separate queries. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both miss and both create, leaving duplicate credentials where later reads use findFirst arbitrarily. It should use an atomic upsert or transaction.

Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts uses prisma.credential.update at line 96 but never imports prisma. Every Salesforce getClient call will throw ReferenceError and break all Salesforce calendar operations, and TypeScript build fails.

Mutating webhook allows any HTTP method

The app-credential webhook creates/overwrites user credentials but never checks req.method. GET, HEAD and other methods can mutate state, exposing encrypted keys in logs/caches and enabling CSRF. It should reject non-POST with 405.

Overwrites expiry_date even when sync returns it

Office365 video always sets expiry_date from expires_in with fallback 0. If the sync endpoint returns expiry_date instead of expires_in, the valid expiry is overwritten with approximately Date.now(), causing immediate expiry and a refresh loop. It should preserve an existing expiry_date.

Sharing flag is string not boolean

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is assigned process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which is a string or undefined, not a boolean. Strict boolean checks will misbehave. It should be coerced with Boolean or !!.

Sync fetch has no auth, no error check and no fallback

refreshOAuthTokens POSTs calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no secret/HMAC, no Content-Type, no response.ok check and no fallback to direct provider refresh. If the endpoint is down or returns an error, refresh fails even though the provider would succeed, causing availability regression, and the unauthenticated callback is spoofable.

Sync response fed to Lark-specific error parser

Lark refresh passes the result of refreshOAuthTokens to handleLarkError which expects a Lark envelope {code:0,data:{...}}. The sync endpoint is documented to return only access_token and expiry, so the parser will throw even on success, breaking Lark refresh when sync is enabled. Sync path needs separate parsing.

Sync response treated as HubspotToken without parsing

Hubspot refresh expects a HubspotToken object from hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. The code then reads .expiresIn/.accessToken directly from the Response and computes expiryDate as NaN, storing invalid tokens and breaking Hubspot integration.

Webhook header lookup not normalized to lowercase

Node lowercases incoming header names, but the code looks up req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] verbatim. If the operator configures an uppercase header name the lookup always misses and all valid webhooks return 403. The env value should be lowercased before lookup.

Wrong appSlug sent to sync endpoint for Zoom

Zoom refresh passes appSlug 'zoomvideo' but the DB appId and credential type use 'zoom' and 'zoom_video'. All other services pass the DB slug. The sync endpoint receiving 'zoomvideo' will not match the Zoom app and cannot return tokens, breaking Zoom refresh in sync mode. It should be 'zoom'.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest deduplication and blacklist bypass via case/whitespace

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-77, filtering does guest === attendee.email and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) where the blacklist is lowercased but guest is not normalized or trimmed. Email comparison is therefore case-sensitive. Consequence: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS can be bypassed with different casing (e.g. Foo@spam.com vs foo@spam.com) and duplicate Attendee rows differing only by case/whitespace can be created, causing duplicate invites and blacklist evasion.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 46, isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). This requires the caller to be both admin and owner at the same time. Since those roles are exclusive, pure admins (and pure owners depending on helper semantics) will always fail the check and be denied even when they should be allowed. Consequence: legitimate team admins/owners who are not the organizer/attendee cannot add guests; authorization is broken.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sends original guests list instead of filtered uniqueGuests to mailer

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 168, the handler inserts only uniqueGuests into the database but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered input. The mailer in packages/emails/email-manager.ts uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide between full scheduled email vs add-guests email. Consequence: pre-existing attendees re-submitted in the request are misclassified as new guests and receive the wrong template, and filtering intent is lost.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
No server-side deduplication of emails within one request

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts around line 92, the server schema is only z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check, and the handler only filters against existing attendees, not within the input itself. A payload like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the filter twice and is inserted via createMany as two Attendee rows. Consequence: duplicate attendee records, duplicate calendar invitees and duplicate emails, corrupting guest counts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add-guests emails ignore disableStandardEmails setting

In packages/emails/email-manager.ts line 525, sendAddGuestsEmails takes only (calEvent, newGuests) and unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails, unlike sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails and others which check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Consequence: event types or workspaces that disabled standard host/attendee emails will still send add-guests notifications, violating user settings.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar update uses requestor credentials instead of organizer

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 158, credentials are loaded via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager is built from the requestor, even though the booking query already includes booking.user credentials and organizer info. If a team admin or attendee adds guests, the external calendar update runs with calendars that do not own the event. Consequence: updateCalendarAttendees fails or updates the wrong calendar, leaving external calendars out of sync while the database was already mutated.

No booking status/time guard before adding guests

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts after line 44, there is no check of booking.status, startTime or endTime before inserting attendees, updating the external calendar, and sending emails. Consequence: callers can add guests to cancelled, rejected, or long-past bookings, triggering calendar updates and confusing add-guests emails for dead events.

Unbounded guests array allows bulk insert/email abuse

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts line 5, guests is defined as z.array(z.string().email()) with no min, max, or uniqueness limit. Consequence: a single authenticated call can submit hundreds or thousands of emails, causing a large createMany, many getTranslation lookups, a huge calendar update payload, and fan-out of emails — enabling spam and DoS.

Validation error flag never cleared on success

In apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx around line 36, onSuccess resets the email list and closes the dialog but does not reset isInvalidEmail, while Cancel does. Consequence: after one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog still shows the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry count increment is not atomic

In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts both failure paths do prisma.workflowReminder.update with data {retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1} using the value read earlier in findMany. Overlapping cron executions can read the same stale value and both write back the same incremented value, losing a count and allowing more retries than the intended limit of 2. Use atomic update {retryCount:{increment:1}} instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders

In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the leading prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany uses OR: [{method:SMS, scheduledDate<=now}, {retryCount:{gt:1}}]. The second branch has no method filter, so it matches EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminders as well as SMS. Only the SMS path increments retryCount today, but any non-SMS row that ever reaches retryCount 2 will be silently deleted, losing the reminder and suppressing the notification. Fix by adding method: SMS (and scheduled:false) to the retryCount branch.

false_positives.candidate:
Failure-handler update can throw and prevent response

In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the catch block does await prisma.workflowReminder.update to bump retryCount with no inner error handling. If that update itself fails (row just deleted by the leading deleteMany in a concurrent run, booking/step deleted, transient DB error, P2025 not-found), the exception escapes the handler, no HTTP response is sent, and the cron run fails. Wrap the cleanup update in its own try/catch or use updateMany and always return a response.

Reminders with missing phone/message never increment retryCount

In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the loop only updates the DB inside if (message?.length && message?.length>0 && sendTo). If sendTo is missing (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or the rendered message is empty, the code does nothing: scheduled stays false and retryCount is unchanged. That same row is returned again by the unscheduledReminders query on every cron tick until scheduledDate ages out (up to 7 days), defeating the new 2-retry limit and causing unbounded reprocessing. false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with === never equal, full-day unavailable override ignored

In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an unavailable-day override where start equals end. `===` on Dayjs objects compares object identity, never value equality, so it is always false. As a result a date override that should block the whole day sets dateOverrideExist but never matches the find, falls through to `if (dateOverrideExist) return true`, and the slot is reported as available when the host is unavailable, allowing bookings on blocked days.

false_positives.candidate:

After scanning dateOverrides, if any override covers the slot day the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` immediately. That early return skips the later `busy.every(...)` calendar/booking check. On any day with a date override, existing Cal bookings, calendar busy blocks, and selected-slot holds for that fixed host are ignored, so double-bookings become possible on override days.

Date-override timezone used without fallback and via toString round-trip

When timeZone is missing, tz gets undefined and produces an invalid/NaN offset or throws, breaking slot generation for legacy overrides. Even when present, `override.start.toString()` serializes the instant in server-local format and re-parses it before converting, which is locale-dependent and fragile compared to using the Date directly with a fallback to organizerTimeZone.

The PR description claims it fixes date overrides of fixed hosts being ignored for round-robin events, which is implemented in the new checkIfIsAvailable filtering in viewer/slots.ts. The only test added covers the same UTC slots under a different invitee timezone for a single-user event. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event, fixed vs loose hosts, and conflicting date overrides, so the main claimed fix and the new working-hours/date-override branches are untested and regressions would not be caught.

The code uses `workingHours.find(h => slot outside h)` to decide the slot is outside working hours. If a user has two intervals in one day, e.g. morning and afternoon, a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon interval, so `find` succeeds and the valid slot is rejected. Conversely if no interval lists that weekday, `find` returns undefined and the code falls through to the busy check, treating a non-working day as available. Valid slots are hidden and invalid days can appear bookable.

The restart path guards cleanup with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), where multiprocessing.Process is the default-context (fork) Process class on Linux and is not a base class of SpawnProcess, so the check is False. As a result when _ensure_processes_alive detects a dead/hung process it calls _create_process_for_shards without killing the old process. A hung process keeps flushing the same Redis shards while the replacement also flushes them, causing duplicate Kafka produces, Redis contention, fd/pid leaks and unbounded process growth. The same isinstance guard in join() prevents terminate() of hung spawn processes on shutdown.

true_positives.golden_comment: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mocked sleep makes flush wait a no-op, test is racy

The test replaces time.sleep with lambda _: None, then after advancing current_drift calls time.sleep(0.1) intending to give background flusher threads time to flush. Because sleep is mocked the wait does nothing. join() sets stopped=True immediately, so whether the flusher flushes before exiting is a race. The test can flakily pass/fail and does not deterministically verify multiprocessed flushing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

false_positives.candidate:
--flusher-processes accepts invalid values that crash consumer

The new --flusher-processes click Option defaults to 1 with type=int and no range validation, so 0 or negative values are accepted and passed as max_processes to SpanFlusher. In the flusher that leads to zero/negative num_processes, which crashes with ZeroDivisionError/KeyError or silently creates no flusher processes. The CLI should reject values <1.

Zero/negative process count crashes or disables flushing

num_processes is computed as min(max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) where max_processes is max_processes or len(...). If assigned_shards is empty on rebalance, or max_processes is 0/negative, num_processes becomes 0 or negative. That yields an empty process_to_shards_map and then i % self.num_processes raises ZeroDivisionError for 0, or i % -1 returns 0 and raises KeyError because the map is empty. With 0 processes submit/record/backpressure loops become no-ops so segments are never flushed, causing silent data loss instead of a clear startup error.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.
The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.

false_positives.candidate:
Closing one strategy shuts down factory-shared queue pool

FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared by every strategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and join() call queue_pool.shutdown() which stops all workers and shuts down all queues. After a Kafka rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy and creates a new one reusing the same dead pool, so subsequent processing stalls or raises and the consumer never recovers without restart. Pool lifetime must be owned by the factory, strategy close should not destroy it.

Each strategy leaks a commit thread sharing one tracker with stale commits

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__ starts its own background commit thread polling the shared factory-level OffsetTracker. On rebalance the old strategy's thread is never stopped by ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown and terminate() does not join it, so multiple threads poll the same tracker and invoke different captured commit callables, including revoked-partition commits, causing duplicate commits, commits via invalid closures, and thread leaks.

Non-atomic partition lock creation breaks mutual exclusion

OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock does get then setdefault on partition_locks without holding a global lock. Two threads submitting/completing/committing the same Partition concurrently can each create a different threading.Lock and then guard add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed with different locks. Mutual exclusion is then lost, causing lost offset updates, wrong committable calculation, duplicate processing or skipping offsets. Use a single global lock to protect lock creation and dict access.

Offsets committed from background thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop invokes the Arroyo commit callable from a dedicated daemon thread every second instead of from poll/join. Arroyo Commit is expected to be called from the processing thread and is not safe to call concurrently with rebalance/shutdown, risking commits for revoked partitions, races with StreamProcessor shutdown, and lost or mis-ordered commits. Commits should happen synchronously in poll/join.

Shutdown abandons queued work instead of draining

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets every worker.shutdown=True before shutting down queues, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. Workers therefore exit immediately even when queues still contain submitted WorkItems. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() thus discards pending work, leaving offsets never completed to be redelivered in bulk or, if already partially committed, losing ordering guarantees. Shutdown should let workers drain via queue shutdown without a separate flag.

Unbounded work queues allow unbounded memory growth

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while poll() only emits metrics. If workers are slow the consumer keeps pulling from Kafka and enqueuing WorkItem objects holding full Messages, growing memory without bound until OOM, contrary to the docstring claim of natural backpressure. Use bounded queues with blocking submit or explicit backpressure.

decode_payload asserts on FilteredPayload instead of skipping

ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload asserts not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload), but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes message.payload which can be FilteredPayload. Every filtered message then raises AssertionError, logs Error submitting message to queue, and only gets skipped via the generic exception path. Filtered payloads are normal and should return None without an exception.

wait_until_empty and stats miss in-flight work

get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize(), which counts only items waiting in the queue, not the item a worker already removed via get() and is still processing. wait_until_empty can return True while workers are still handling results, and total_queued metrics undercount load. Callers using it to decide completion or shutdown can proceed prematurely. Track outstanding work via OffsetTracker outstanding counts or task_done/unfinished_tasks instead of qsize.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Every cached deny triggers DB fetch, nullifying permission cache

After a denial-cache miss, Check loads cached permissions; if they hit but checkPermission returns false it falls through to getIdentityPermissions which queries the DB for identifiers, roles, teams and permissions. Previously a cached scope map served denies without DB work. Now every Check for a distinct resource the user lacks access to costs full DB queries, with the per-resource denial cache only helping repeats of the exact same name+parent. Enumerating many random names or normal deny-heavy traffic causes one DB permission fetch per distinct resource. Consequence: large latency and DB load regression and easy DoS amplification.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Denial key concatenation ambiguous, distinct resources share entry

The denial key is namespace + '.perm_' + userUID + '_' + action + '_' + name + '_' + parent with plain underscore separators and no escaping. Different tuples collide, for example name 'a_b' with parent 'c' produces the same suffix as name 'a' with parent 'b_c', and UIDs or actions containing underscores add more collisions. Since dashboard/folder UIDs can contain underscores, two distinct resources can map to the same denial key. Consequence: a denial cached for one resource falsely denies an unrelated resource for up to the TTL.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

false_positives.candidate:
DB fallback reuses stale team and role caches, missing new team grants

getUserPermissions, used for the fallback DB read, first calls getUserBasicRole and getUserTeams which return cached values when present. The subsequent permissionStore.GetUserPermissions query is built from those possibly stale team IDs and role. If access was newly granted via team membership or basic-role change, the fallback still queries with old teams/role and returns no permission, so Check denies and caches denial. Consequence: requerying permissions from the DB does not fix freshness for team/role-driven grants until those caches expire.

Denial cache key omits identity type, poisoning across principals

userPermDenialCacheKey builds a key from namespace, userUID, action, name and parent only, with no identity type. Anonymous subject 'anonymous:0' and render subject 'render:0' both resolve to UID '0', so they share the identical denial key for the same namespace/action/resource. Service.Check checks this denial cache first and returns Allowed:false on hit without evaluating permissions. Consequence: a denial cached for anonymous causes a later renderer check for the same dashboard/folder to be denied without ever consulting renderer wildcard logic, and any user/service-account UID overlap across types shares the same fate, causing false denies for up to the 30s TTL.

Denial cache short-circuits fresh DB read, preserving stale denies

Check looks up permDenialCache and on hit immediately returns Allowed:false without consulting cached permissions or the database. Denial entries are set after a DB-backed deny and live 30 seconds with no invalidation. If access is granted after the denial was cached, for example a newly created dashboard/folder grant or role change, checks for that same name+folder within the TTL still deny even though the DB would now allow. This defeats the PR's own fallback that requeries the DB when cached scopes miss, because the denial hit prevents that fallback. Consequence: newly granted access remains invisible until expiry.

Folder hierarchy cache not refreshed on deny, breaking inherited grants

checkInheritedPermissions calls buildFolderTree which returns the cached folderTree if present and otherwise never refreshes it on permission denial. Check's new fallback refreshes permission scopes from the DB but leaves the folder tree stale. If a child folder or dashboard is created under a parent the user can access, the stale tree lacks the new node so Ancestors/Children lookups still fail, the check denies even with fresh scopes and then caches a per-resource denial. Consequence: new nested folders/dashboards relying on inherited folder permissions stay inaccessible until the folder cache expires.

List serves stale cached permissions with no outdated-cache fallback

List calls getCachedIdentityPermissions and if it hits uses that scope map directly to build the response, only querying the DB on cache miss. Unlike Check there is no revalidation when the cached map is outdated. If the per-user/action permCache entry was populated before a dashboard/folder was created or granted, List omits the new item until the 30s entry expires. Consequence: the stated goal of letting users fetch newly created dashboards/folders still fails on the List path.

true_positives.golden_comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

true_positives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules

RuleActionsButtons sets showSilenceDrawer true when Silence is clicked from AlertRuleMenu, which now appears via Grafana prom abilities, but the drawer is only rendered if rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where rule is the optional ruler rule. In the prom-only list view rule is undefined, so the condition is always false and clicking Silence notifications does nothing with no error.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete action can never show in prom-only list view

AlertRuleMenu computes canDelete as OR of ruler and Grafana prom abilities, but rendering is gated on canDelete && rulerRule. In the new list view only promRule is passed and rulerRule is undefined, so Delete never appears even for users with delete permission. The computed Grafana delete ability is dead code and delete is regressed.

Federated rule protection removed

The old useAllAlertRuleAbilities checked isFederatedRuleGroup to mark federated groups immutable and block Update/Delete/Pause. The new useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated to false with a TODO. Federated Mimir rules now appear editable, removable and pausable in the UI, allowing users to attempt mutations that should be blocked.

Newly created rules disappear until Prometheus syncs

GrafanaGroupLoader previously merged ruler and Prometheus and rendered ruler-only rules as Creating and prom-only rules as Deleting to hide eventual consistency. It now renders only promResponse rules. A rule just created in the ruler but not yet in Prometheus vanishes from the list instead of showing Creating, and recently deleted rules appear as normal, confusing users and inviting duplicate creates or repeated edits.

Pause action can never show in prom-only list view

AlertRuleMenu computes canPause as OR of ruler and Grafana prom abilities, implying prom-only rules should be pausable, but rendering additionally requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) to be truthy. In the new list view rulerRule is undefined, so the Pause menu item never renders even when the user has pause permission. Users lose Pause from the list view.

Rule view link drops returnTo navigation

The previous GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href with createReturnTo and passed returnTo as a query param so the detail page can navigate back to the filtered list. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds href as /alerting/grafana/<uid>/view without returnTo, so Back navigation from the rule view loses list context.

skipToken still grants Duplicate for non-Grafana rules

useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities maps skipToken to undefined and calls useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). For undefined the hook still returns supported=true for Duplicate based on Grafana create permission. ORed with ruler abilities in AlertRuleMenu, this shows Duplicate for data-source rules to users who have Grafana rule create but lack external write permission, over-exposing the action.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

false_positives.candidate:
Double interpolation duplicates ad-hoc filters

runShardSplitQuery interpolates with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery via subRequest={...request, targets:...} which interpolates again with the same scopedVars/filters. The updated test expecting 5 calls for 1 target confirms the double pass. Applying template variables with request.filters rewrites expr to add ad-hoc filters; running it twice appends them twice and re-expands variables, producing over-constrained/wrong LogQL and wasted work. Interpolation with filters should happen once.

Early interpolation defeats $__range split guard and freezes range

runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target before querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable is checked. applyTemplateVariables expands template variables (new test proves it expands $__auto and $step), so it will also expand $__range/$__range_s/$__range_ms before the guard sees them. The guard !isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) will then pass and a query that must not be split will be split. All split sub-requests will carry $__range/$__interval frozen to the full-range value instead of per-split-range backend interpolation described in the code comment, returning wrong data.

Empty check runs before interpolation

runSplitQuery filters with .filter((query)=>query.expr) before .map((query)=>datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)). A query whose raw expr is truthy but interpolates to empty (e.g. expr is a variable that is empty/undefined) passes the filter and then flows into isLogsQuery/partition/grouping and datasource.runQuery. This issues backend requests for empty queries and can misclassify them. The same pattern exists in shardQuerySplitting.ts. Filter for empty expr after interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request

In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go line 40, QueryData (and similarly CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) dereferences req.PluginContext without checking req for nil. The sibling LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards if req == nil before touching it, showing nil is considered possible. Since ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wired outer to LoggerMiddleware in pluginsintegration.go, a nil request panics with nil dereference before reaching Logger's guard, crashing the request path.

true_positives.golden_comment: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Plugin request logs no longer include traceID

In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go line 49, logRequest builds logParams with only status, duration, eventName and time_before_plugin_request. The old code explicitly added traceID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext. The new code removed that and relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The context enrichment in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname, never traceID. So traceID is silently dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' logs, breaking trace-to-log correlation for plugin requests.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestLogger.FromContext discards logs

In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go line 46, TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a fresh empty logger, ignoring the receiver. The real implementation in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go returns a wrapper sharing the underlying sink with contextual attributes. After the change LoggerMiddleware does m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so the Info call lands on the throwaway object, not on the injected m.logger. Tests asserting on the original TestLogger's InfoLogs/WarnLogs will see zero calls, making the new logging path unobservable and untestable.

false_positives.candidate:
FromContext silently drops context on type assertion failure

In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go line 48, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext asserts d.l.FromContext(ctx) to *log.ConcreteLogger and on failure returns d.New(), a fresh logger with no contextual attributes. That silently discards endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, with no error or fallback to the original logger. If the infra logger ever returns a different Logger implementation, plugin request logs lose all context invisibly.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert race allows exceeding the device limit

CreateOrUpdateDevice in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go does CountDevices, then if count < deviceLimit falls through to INSERT. There is no transaction, row lock, or unique count constraint. Two concurrent new devices when count == limit-1 can both observe count < limit and both INSERT different device_ids, ending with limit+1 active devices. Under load, when the limit matters most, it is unenforceable. Fix with atomic guard e.g. serializable transaction, conditional insert, or DB-side enforcement.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache poisoning lets any new device bypass the device limit on retry

tagDeviceUI in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go checks localCache, then calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the DB returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry is already stored and never removed. The next request for the same deviceID hits the cache early-return nil, so TagDevice succeeds and Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds. Any blocked device can therefore get anonymous access by making a second request, and transient DB errors also cause permanent 29-minute under-counting. Fix by caching only after successful DB write or evicting on failure.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Anonymous tagging moved from background to synchronous auth hot path

Anonymous.Authenticate in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go previously tagged devices in a go routine with context.Background and 2-minute timeout and never blocked login. This PR calls anonDeviceService.TagDevice synchronously with the request ctx, which on cache miss does CountDevices plus INSERT/UPDATE. Every new anonymous login now pays extra DB round-trips and inherits DB slowness/failure, coupling login availability and p99 latency to the anon_device table. Fix by keeping tagging async/off-request or using detached context with timeout for the non-limit path.

No test that existing devices can still update when at limit

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go only verifies a second distinct deviceID gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never verifies the intended allow-path that an already-counted deviceID can still be updated when count >= limit, nor expiry-window or cache interaction. A regression breaking legitimate returning devices would not be caught. Add a test that re-tags the first device after the limit is reached and expects success and updated timestamp.

Provider signature change breaks DI wiring and testability

ProvideAnonymousDeviceService in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go changed from taking anonstore.AnonStore to taking db.DB and constructing ProvideAnonDBStore internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. No wire_gen update is in the PR, so existing generated code passing an AnonStore will fail to compile. It also hard-codes the DB implementation, preventing mocks/fakes or alternate stores. Fix by regenerating wire, or keep injecting AnonStore and inject the limit separately.

Unlimited limit sent as 0 mismatches frontend undefined contract

FrontendSettingsDTO in pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go adds AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 with json:"anonymousDeviceLimit" and no omitempty, so unlimited (0 in Cfg) serializes as 0. Frontend types declare anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined with default undefined. After lodash merge, 0 overwrites undefined, so UI cannot distinguish unlimited from a zero-device limit if it checks for undefined. Use pointer with omitempty or document that 0 means unlimited on both sides.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Routine cleanup logs at Error level with full ID lists

pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go logs normal cleanup progress with r.log.Error at lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579, including the full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs) and cond on every batch even on success. true_positives.golden_comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup ticker changed from 10m to 1m without justification

pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go line 77 changes the background cleanup ticker from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1. This makes all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) run 10x more often. true_positives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete drops structured log values from context

In DualWriterMode3.Delete the code builds log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method) but then does ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of using log. true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage duration

In DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection the background goroutine calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection but then calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete success records object name as kind label

In DualWriterMode3.Delete success path the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where name is the object name, while every other call passes options.Kind as the kind label. Consequence: per-object high-cardinality values pollute a Prometheus kind label, causing metric cardinality explosion and useless kind breakdowns.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy backup inherits cancellable request context

Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection all do go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ; d.Legacy.*(ctx, ...) } where ctx is the incoming request context. After the API handler returns the request context is cancelled, so the derived context is immediately Done and the 10s timeout does not help. Create storage error recorded as legacy duration

In DualWriterMode3.Create, when Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of d.recordStorageDuration. The timed interval is the storage call, not a legacy call, and no legacy call was made. Consequence: storage failures are invisible in storage metrics and falsely inflate legacy error metrics, hiding unified-storage outages.

Legacy async write reuses mutable input without copy

In Create the code returns created to the caller while a goroutine concurrently reads obj, options and createValidation via d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, createValidation, options). Even without aliasing, legacy gets the pre-storage object without storage-assigned UID/resourceVersion. Update has the same flaw by re-invoking objInfo for legacy instead of reusing the storage result res, so legacy computes a different object from a different old state. Mode3 tests never verify async legacy writes

TestMode3_Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection share one mock.Mock between legacy and storage mocks, return immediately without waiting for the background goroutine, and never assert legacy was called. Update storage error recorded as legacy duration

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock causes redundant reloads

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45-48 GetWebAssets implements double-checked locking incorrectly: it checks entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, releases it, then takes the write Lock without re-checking. If two goroutines both observe nil (cold start) or race a Dev/Prod transition, both will sequentially execute readWebAssetsFromFile and the second overwrites the first. Consequence is N expensive manifest parses and file reads instead of one, plus possible inconsistency if the file changes between reads. After acquiring the write lock it should re-check if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil and return early.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() with defer Unlock() and then performs disk I/O in readWebAssetsFromFile and potentially network I/O in readWebAssetsFromCDN while still holding the exclusive lock. The lock should only guard pointer publication: read outside the lock then Lock, re-check, and swap.

When the storage backend closes the stream the loop receives nil forever and panics on dereference, and if the broadcaster stops the send blocks forever and leaks the goroutine.

In searchSupport.init each errgroup worker runs `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` where both variables are shared across workers without synchronization. Concurrent increments lose counts and concurrent assignments to the outer err race, so one worker can overwrite another's error before it is returned and the race detector will flag it. Use a local err variable inside the closure and an atomic counter.

Eager Init leaks cancel and blocks startup with no timeout

NewResourceServer creates a cancelable server context then calls s.Init synchronously. On Init failure it returns nil and error without calling cancel, leaking the context. true_positives.matched_candidate:

Example: grant view on client A creating its resource, then grant manage on all clients. A check for manage on A finds A's resource, sees only view, and denies despite the all-clients manage grant. Both the specific and the type resources must be evaluated with OR semantics.

Mutual exclusion is then lost, causing lost offset updates, wrong committable calculation, duplicate processing or skipping offsets. Use a single global lock to protect lock creation and dict access.

Unbounded work queues allow unbounded memory growth

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while poll() only emits metrics. If workers are slow the consumer keeps pulling from Kafka and enqueuing WorkItem objects holding full Messages, growing memory without bound until OOM, contrary to the docstring claim of natural backpressure. Use bounded queues with blocking submit or explicit backpressure.

Closing one strategy shuts down factory-shared queue pool

FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared by every strategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and join() call queue_pool.shutdown() which stops all workers and shuts down all queues. After a Kafka rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy and creates a new one reusing the same dead pool, so subsequent processing stalls or raises and the consumer never recovers without restart. Pool lifetime must be owned by the factory, strategy close should not destroy it.

Each strategy leaks a commit thread sharing one tracker with stale commits

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__ starts its own background commit thread polling the shared factory-level OffsetTracker. On rebalance the old strategy's thread is never stopped by ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown and terminate() does not join it, so multiple threads poll the same tracker and invoke different captured commit callables, including revoked-partition commits, causing duplicate commits, commits via invalid closures, and thread leaks.

Offsets committed from background thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop invokes the Arroyo commit callable from a dedicated daemon thread every second instead of from poll/join. Arroyo Commit is expected to be called from the processing thread and is not safe to call concurrently with rebalance/shutdown, risking commits for revoked partitions, races with StreamProcessor shutdown, and lost or mis-ordered commits. Commits should happen synchronously in poll/join.

Shutdown abandons queued work instead of draining

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets every worker.shutdown=True before shutting down queues, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. Workers therefore exit immediately even when queues still contain submitted WorkItems. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() thus discards pending work, leaving offsets never completed to be redelivered in bulk or, if already partially committed, losing ordering guarantees. Shutdown should let workers drain via queue shutdown without a separate flag.

decode_payload asserts on FilteredPayload instead of skipping

ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload asserts not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload), but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes message.payload which can be FilteredPayload. Every filtered message then raises AssertionError, logs Error submitting message to queue, and only gets skipped via the generic exception path. Filtered payloads are normal and should return None without an exception.

get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize(), which counts only items waiting in the queue, not the item a worker already removed via get() and is still processing. wait_until_empty can return True while workers are still handling results, and total_queued metrics undercount load. true_positives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.

After a denial-cache miss, Check loads cached permissions; if they hit but checkPermission returns false it falls through to getIdentityPermissions which queries the DB for identifiers, roles, teams and permissions. Now every Check for a distinct resource the user lacks access to costs full DB queries, with the per-resource denial cache only helping repeats of the exact same name+parent. Enumerating many random names or normal deny-heavy traffic causes one DB permission fetch per distinct resource. Consequence: large latency and DB load regression and easy DoS amplification.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. Denial key concatenation ambiguous, distinct resources share entry

The denial key is namespace + '.perm_' + userUID + '_' + action + '_' + name + '_' + parent with plain underscore separators and no escaping. Different tuples collide, for example name 'a_b' with parent 'c' produces the same suffix as name 'a' with parent 'b_c', and UIDs or actions containing underscores add more collisions. Since dashboard/folder UIDs can contain underscores, two distinct resources can map to the same denial key. Consequence: a denial cached for one resource falsely denies an unrelated resource for up to the TTL.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify ambiguous underscore-separated cache key concatenation that allows distinct component tuples to collide, causing incorrect denial cache hits and false permission denials.

Service.Check checks this denial cache first and returns Allowed:false on hit without evaluating permissions. Consequence: a denial cached for anonymous causes a later renderer check for the same dashboard/folder to be denied without ever consulting renderer wildcard logic, and any user/service-account UID overlap across types shares the same fate, causing false denies for up to the 30s TTL.

If access is granted after the denial was cached, for example a newly created dashboard/folder grant or role change, checks for that same name+folder within the TTL still deny even though the DB would now allow. This defeats the PR's own fallback that requeries the DB when cached scopes miss, because the denial hit prevents that fallback. Consequence: newly granted access remains invisible until expiry.

If a child folder or dashboard is created under a parent the user can access, the stale tree lacks the new node so Ancestors/Children lookups still fail, the check denies even with fresh scopes and then caches a per-resource denial. If access was newly granted via team membership or basic-role change, the fallback still queries with old teams/role and returns no permission, so Check denies and caches denial. Consequence: requerying permissions from the DB does not fix freshness for team/role-driven grants until those caches expire.
